answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. The protocol caps how much one identity can influence a market, so an attacker must split funds across many identities and lock proportionally more tokens to gain sway. A spiral of fake accounts is therefore costly: capital stays unavailable for legitimate use and risks slashing if accounts collude or break rules. The lagoon and comet markets can still admit new agents, but creating identities no longer creates influence for free.
